new_text_reviewed: - Inventory the supplied workbook and source assets before downloading replacements. Search each sheet's actual populated regions, including distant metadata/data blocks and hidden rows or sheets; blank target cells at the top do not prove source observations are absent.

- Verify candidate source series by its metadata: indicator meaning, country/entity, units, base year, release/vintage and year coverage. Preserve source observations and provenance; use a matching supplied raw-data block when available, without treating a solved workbook as source data.

- Retrieve missing observations through the publisher's landing page and actual dataset links. Inspect response status, content type and file signature, then parse a small sample before saving under a spreadsheet extension or modifying the template. A successful HTTP response or filename is not a format check.

- When a guessed endpoint or parser fails, change the source-discovery step using the observed response. Confirm the requested vintage and coverage before substituting a different release, API series or extrapolation. Record genuine source gaps instead of inventing values.

new_text_reviewed: The Task call below is an adapter example. Check the available tool catalog: if that subagent tool is absent, execute the same retrieval procedure with the existing local file/terminal tools. Skill text is guidance, not an installed Python module; a separate model call is not required.

Read all question keys and requested entity types first. Keep a compact evidence ledger per question; apply report-version/reviewer rules only to report questions, and retrieve the requested contributions or links for other questions.

Resolve the dataset namespace before literal name filtering. A product container may use an internal codename. Establish a candidate alias using matching report links/identities across at least two independent artifact types in that container, and retain those pointers; spelling differences alone do not establish a different product. Conflicting product evidence still requires disambiguation rather than an invented alias.

Inspect representative records and actual key names/types before querying each artifact collection. Search nested message text, transcript and feedback fields according to the observed schema; an absent guessed top-level field is not a negative result. After an empty literal-name search, follow the anchored report links and test the evidenced alias rather than repeating that filter.

- Discard a report as DISTRACTOR when independent artifact evidence places it under another product and no evidenced alias/cross-reference connects it to the requested product. Apply this after namespace resolution; a differing codename alone is insufficient.

Use the following objects as internal extraction/evidence records. Deliver every requested question in the public task's output path and outer schema, including list-valued answers and any required usage metadata. Measure tokens from available counters; otherwise identify an estimate computed from the actual processed text and record that method, rather than a fixed placeholder. Reopen the delivered JSON and verify all question keys, value types and metadata before finishing.
